content: Twinfilin-1 is a protein in humans encoded by the TWF1 gene. This gene produces twinfilin, a protein that binds to actin monomers and is evolutionarily conserved across species, from yeast to mammals. Research on the mouse version of this protein indicates that it may function as an actin monomer-binding protein. Its localization to structures rich in cortical G-actin appears to be regulated by the small GTPase RAC1. To study the function of TWF1, model organisms have been utilized. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Twf1tm1a(EUCOMM)Wtsi, was created as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a large-scale mutagenesis initiative aimed at generating and distributing animal models of human diseases to researchers. The knockout mice, both male and female, underwent a standardized series of phenotypic tests to assess the impact of the gene deletion. A total of 23 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, but no significant abnormalities were identified.
